neighbours.secrets: The mobeds who carried Adur Farnbag from Khwarazm to Mount Kavarvand are still alive there, through the Gifts of Gayomart, and a living Mazdean community shelters in the higher levels of Naw Bahar's regio. The most devout mobeds still know the rite of Saoshyant's Elixir, the faith's road to a life without end.

neighbours.name: Ashab al-Najm, the Followers of the Star
neighbours.summary:
The family of Solomonic Astrology. It began with a handful of Zoroastrian converts who came to Baghdad to learn from al-Khwarizmi, al-Fazari's pupil, and went on to found a small academy at Nasibin in the north and houses given wholly to the stars in many Persian cities. It is the most widespread of the families and the most arcane: its sahirs look and dress the part of the wise magician, and hold that magic must keep its grandeur in the people's eyes even as it serves them.

Its seat, the House of the Heavens at Nasibin, emptied in 1186 when its Asala and vizier led every sahir of the city away; the family's astrologers have since travelled in caravans with their laboratories, most of them still in Jazira. Meriq of Savah has led it since.

Story seeds:
The Astrologer's Spirit: many sahirs think al-Fazari never died but became a spirit, as his father did; whoever could summon him would learn what his prophetic pictures foretold, but no one has shown they can.

neighbours.name: Ashab al-Yad, the Followers of the Hand
neighbours.summary:
The family of Solomonic Physic, begun by the Bakhtyshu physicians, who carried their art to Gundeshapur and its House of Healing. Its first members were Nestorian Christians, and it has always taken in Muslims, Jews and pagans alike; that openness has given it a poor name among the sahirs, who see in it a family that can harm as readily as it heals, and never quite know which a Follower of the Hand will do.

Story seeds:
A Son in the Far East: some say one of Jabril ibn Bakhtyshu's sons went east with the miracle-worker Dawud al-Kharita and began a line of Christian magician-kings that would give the world Prester John.

neighbours.name: Ashab al-Qalb, the Followers of the Heart
neighbours.summary:
The family of Solomonic Storytelling. Al-Zill Habib, the 'beloved shadow', founded it, but so little is known of him that its sahirs look instead to al-Khayzuran as their mother and model. Its art has stayed rooted in Baghdad, the city of a thousand tales, and most grand viziers have come from it, Kha'trazh among them. Its sahirs are political, deal with faeries and magical beings more than the other families do, are seldom Gifted, and are nearly as often women as men.

Its Asala is old; Niya of the Dar al-Hikma is expected to follow him.

Story seeds:
The Lady of the Vanished Chamber: sahirs who feel for spirits sense a woman's presence in Al-Khayzuran's old room in what was Harun's palace, and many dream of her; perhaps the tales told of her have drawn a faerie queen to live there, who trades power to sleepers for stories.

neighbours.name: Ashab al-Halqa, the Followers of the Circle
neighbours.summary:
Not a recognised family but a name for sahirs who follow none of the five arts, or who put their summoning first. The sahirs of Cordoba used it before they left the Order, after the rim of the pentacle in Solomon's Seal. Most Gifted sahirs and self-taught summoners count among them; they keep away from the Majlis, where viziers of the other families must speak for them. Some draw the Seal with six points, to claim Sihr as a sixth art and their own, and a movement among them asks for a sixth Asala.

The Cordoban sahirs who joined the Order of Hermes in 925 are the Hermetic Sahirs of Houses of Hermes: Societates, Followers of the Circle within House Ex Miscellanea.

Story seeds:
The Sixth Asala: sahirs outside the five families demand a sixth seat among the Asalat, and take a six-pointed star as their sign.

details.wants: A sixth Asala, and Sihr counted as a sixth Solomonic art.

neighbours.name: The Hall of the Majlis
neighbours.summary:
A great six-sided hall at the heart of Baghdad's summer bazaar, where the Order of Suleiman meets. Magic hides it: from outside it is only a cluster of bright tents that always seem further off, and spirits the Asalat summon guard it. Within, tiers of cushions, lamps and fans descend in six steps, one for each family, under a ceiling that shows the open heavens; conjured servants carry food and drink, and on the stage at the centre, inlaid with a golden pentacle, the grand vizier sits on a jewelled throne.

When autumn comes the fair packs up and the district is left looking like rubble; the local sahirs keep that illusion up all year so that no one stumbles on the hall, and the few traders who stay are in the secret.

Story seeds:
The Sahir-Magus: a magus who can summon spirits is admitted to the Suhhar and offers to speak for his sodales; that threatens Kha'trazh's policy of avoiding a fight with the Order of Hermes, and he may quietly urge other sahirs to challenge the newcomer to a duel.

neighbours.name: The Grand Vizier's Island Fortress
neighbours.summary: A stronghold of stone in the Magic Realm, on an island far out in a cold, empty sea. Sahirs who have met Hermetic magi are brought here to talk with the grand vizier in private, since the war is never discussed at the Majlis, where the enemy might be listening.
neighbours.secrets: A pit at its centre is the Order's prison. The grand vizier is said to hold an Arcane Connection to it, and a Travel ritual of level 45, the Oubliette al-Wazir, opens a way straight there without crossing the Twilight Void, so a traitor can be sent into exile with no one the wiser.

neighbours.name: The House of the Heavens
neighbours.summary:
For most of the Order's life the seat of the Followers of the Star: five great buildings of white stone set round a sixth with an observatory and astrolabe, and in the courtyard between them a procession of statues of the old Babylonian figures for the planets and the signs.

Late in the summer of 1186, soon after its vizier and the Asala al-Najm came home from the Majlis, every sahir of Nasibin left together. Some had packed beforehand; others walked away from unfinished work. Astrologers reckon that all seven planets then stood in Libra, a sign of subtlety, independence and help given to others. Neither leader has been heard of since. Most sahirs think they went to help Salah al-Din at Hattin and the taking of Jerusalem in 1187; others that they set out to be rid of Rashid al-Din Sinan, the Syrian Nizaris' chief. The houses stand empty.

Meriq, the family's Asala, insists that this is still the family's house and that those who left will come back to it.
neighbours.secrets: The book leaves why they went, and whether Meriq is right, to the storyguide.

neighbours.name: The Observatory of Savah
neighbours.summary: The top of the tall domed tower beside Savah's great mosque, above the library, kept by Savah's house of wisdom. It is famous across the world for its star maps, from old Babylon to the present day, and for the newest instruments of the astronomers. Besides its Magic aura of 5, it gives +3 to every astrology roll, Solomonic Astrology included.

neighbours.name: The Halls of the House of Healing
neighbours.summary:
Gundeshapur's great medical school and hospital, founded by the sahir Bakhtyshu of Harun's council and run ever since by his descendants; the Seljuk sultans paid for it and the Khwarazm-shah still honours it. A palatial building near the middle of the town, open on every side under canvas porches on wooden columns, with a great hall ringed by a corridor like a cloister and windows showing the tales of the First Council, which townsfolk take for Christian legends.

A Divine aura lies over the whole house, so its sahirs have dug their laboratories far below.

levels.name: The laboratories beneath
levels.notes: Rooms dug deep under the house, where buried pockets of Magic let the sahirs work; long, narrow ladders lead down to them from the common rooms.

neighbours.name: The Majlis of 1220 and the Succession
neighbours.summary:
Driven by the old grand vizier's mortality and the ambitions of the viziers around him. Kha'trazh has led the Order of Suleiman for nearly thirty years and looks fifty, but he is close to a hundred, and most sahirs expect him to die soon. Whoever succeeds him decides whether the Suhhar keeps its cautious peace with the Order of Hermes or turns its counter-crusade loose.

If he dies between meetings the five Asalat by custom name the vizier of the Dar al-Hikma to act for him. That is Niya, Gifted, young, and convinced that only Gifted sahirs can save a stagnant Order, a view so unpopular that she is unlikely to keep the seat when the viziers vote. The campaign will start the day the old man is buried.

details.antagonist: The viziers who would follow Kha'trazh, and his opponents

stages.title: The Majlis of August
stages.clues: Viziers gather in Baghdad's summer bazaar for the three days of 15 to 17 August 1220. The young 'Arkhaman comes from Sana'a as a new vizier with an Infernal jinni in tow; Nil of Gundeshapur faces accusations again; a sahir Kha'trazh expels becomes a cause for his rivals.
stages.ignored: Kha'trazh hears every speaker, keeps his peace with the magi, and the factions count their friends for next year.
stages.stopped: The meeting ends with the grand vizier's authority whole.
stages.turned: The troupe's own vizier, or a magus sponsored as a sahir, wins a voice at the Majlis.

stages.title: Kha'trazh dies
stages.clues: The grand vizier tires, sleeps through his own councils, or is found dead in his chamber; some will ask whether he was helped.
stages.ignored: The Asalat meet and set Niya in his place until the next Majlis, and her rivals begin to canvass openly.
stages.stopped: A cure or a guardian keeps him alive a few years longer.
stages.turned: The troupe chooses whom the Asalat name to act for him.

stages.title: The election
stages.clues: Candidates court every vizier; one promises to restore an expelled favourite, another a war on the magi; a Follower of the Stone may try to take his family's seat by a test of arms first. All five Asalat must be there, and none may stand.
stages.ignored: A Follower of the Heart is elected by acclaim, and the counter-crusade gains or loses a patron by who it is.
stages.stopped: A candidate who keeps the peace with the magi wins.
stages.turned: The troupe's candidate takes the seat, with all it owes.

links.note: Would act for him; unlikely to keep it
The family of most grand viziers
Picks its Asala by a test of arms

neighbours.name: The Solomonic Counter-Crusade
neighbours.summary:
Driven by the Followers of the Stone, whose Asala first named the crusaders tools of Hell, and by the Syrian viziers. The Order of Suleiman counts itself still at war with the Franks and every Hermetic magus among them. While the Fifth Crusade holds Damietta, its sahirs gather what they can learn of the Order of Hermes: magi are welcomed in the lands of Islam, where they are easy to watch and easy to find again, and are studied for their weak places.

The aim is a blow at the Levant that drives the invading magi out for good. The sahirs know from the First Crusade that open battle with magi goes badly for them, so the attack, when it comes, will use the Magic Realm's roads, the stars' timing and spirits, not ranks of wizards. Kha'trazh has so far held it back.

details.antagonist: The Followers of the Stone and the Syrian viziers who would strike at the Levant

stages.title: Watching the magi
stages.clues: Hospitable strangers ask a visiting magus about his covenant, his sodales and his habits; a summoned spirit follows him home; a sahir offers to guide him anywhere he likes.
stages.ignored: The Suhhar learns which covenants of the Levant are weakest and when their magi are away.
stages.stopped: The spies are found out and the magi warned.
stages.turned: The troupe feeds the watchers what it wants them to believe.

stages.title: Choosing the targets
stages.clues: Stone viziers press the Majlis for leave to act; astrologers look for a favourable conjunction; sahirs teach Solomonic magic to soldiers on the Syrian front, as the old wazirs once did.
stages.ignored: The plan is agreed in private, outside the Majlis.
stages.stopped: The grand vizier forbids it, or a peace between the orders takes its place.
stages.turned: The blow is turned on the Order's real enemies, the Mongols or the Infernal.

stages.title: The strike
stages.clues: Spirits mass in the Magic Realm behind a Levantine covenant.
stages.ignored: A covenant of the Levant is ambushed from the Magic Realm, and its Tribunal calls for war on the sahirs.
stages.stopped: The attack is beaten off, and the sahirs lose face.
stages.turned: The troupe brokers terms before blood is shed.

neighbours.name: Jalal al-Din Hasan's Alliances and the Feud
neighbours.summary:
Driven by Jalal al-Din Hasan, who has led the Nizaris since 1210 and has outwardly made them Sunni, which his followers take for taqiyya. He wants friends against the Khwarazm-shah: he has bound himself to the rulers of Arran and Azarbayjan and wed the emir of Gilan's four daughters, and looks to the caliph in the west and to Genghis Khan in the east.

The Order of Suleiman has not forgiven Hasan-i Sabbah's murder of its grand vizier. It calls the Nizaris traitors, will not treat with them, and hunts known members by turning the crowd's fear on them; the Nizaris kill sahirs only when they stand in the imam's way. Each side's losses have matched the other's for a century, and Nil of Gundeshapur is suspected of standing too close to them.

details.antagonist: Jalal al-Din Hasan, grand master of Alamut

stages.title: Envoys to the caliph and the khan
stages.clues: Nizari envoys travel under false names to Baghdad and toward the Mongol camps; the sahirs' astrologers and spies mark them.
stages.ignored: The imam's new friends make the Nizaris harder for the Suhhar to touch.
stages.stopped: An embassy is waylaid and its letters taken.
stages.turned: The troupe carries the imam's word, and his gratitude.

stages.title: The accusations at the Majlis
stages.clues: Nil's accusers bring word of Nizari visitors to the House of Healing.
stages.ignored: Nil shrugs them off once more, and the feud goes on in the dark.
stages.stopped: The truth of Nil's ties comes out and is settled.
stages.turned: Nil becomes a channel between the two, the first parley in a century.

stages.title: The castles fall
stages.clues: If history holds, the Mongols come for the mountain fortresses.
stages.ignored: The Mongols destroy the Nizari strongholds of Persia, Alamut among them.
stages.stopped: The sect's secret ways keep a castle or two alive.
stages.turned: The sahirs and the Nizaris stand together at last.

neighbours.name: The Succession at Mecca
neighbours.summary:
Driven by al-Hasan, who means to succeed his father Qatada, Grand Sharif of Mecca since 1201, and will not wait. If history holds he takes the city this year by killing Qatada and many of their kin, and the Ayyubid sultan of Yemen, al-Mas'ud Yusuf, marches in to end the chaos and rules Mecca by the sword until he dies.

The holy city's Dominion keeps wizards out, but not their agents, pilgrims or spirits; a sahir or magus who wants a debt from the next Sharif, or a relic from the Haram, has this year to earn it.

details.antagonist: al-Hasan, son of the Grand Sharif Qatada

stages.title: The massacre
stages.clues: Qatada's sons quarrel openly; al-Hasan gathers armed men in the Hijaz; pilgrims hear rumours.
stages.ignored: Qatada and many of his family are killed.
stages.stopped: The Grand Sharif is warned and lives.
stages.turned: The troupe picks the heir who rules.

stages.title: The sultan of Yemen steps in
stages.clues: Al-Mas'ud Yusuf's troops leave Yemen for the north.
stages.ignored: Mecca comes under the Ayyubids' military rule.
stages.stopped: The Sharifs settle their quarrel before he arrives.
stages.turned: The troupe wins the sultan's favour in Mecca.

stages.title: The Sharifs return
stages.clues: If history holds, al-Mas'ud Yusuf dies.
stages.ignored: The Grand Sharifs take Mecca back on his death.

neighbours.name: Azi Dahak Seeks a Host
neighbours.summary:
Driven by Azi Dahak, the three-headed serpent demon who hates Persia and rules it whenever he finds a willing body. The one he possesses becomes a Zahhak: a black snake grows from each shoulder, regrowing however often it is cut, and hungers for human brains. Mohammed al-Ghuri, the Shansabani sultan beaten fourteen years ago, was the most recent; another so soon would be unusual, but the demon is looking.

Some Persian sahirs believe Genghis Khan is a new Zahhak, or listens to one: the way he has turned on Persia is the demon's way. The vanished Shansabani, Zahhak's own line, are rumoured to have an heir at the khan's court. Flame from a Mazdean temple harms the demon, and the first Zahhak, chained alive under Mount Damavand and no longer possessed, may advise those who would fight the next.

details.antagonist: Azi Dahak, Duke of the Spirits of Deceit, and the Shansabani heir

stages.title: Whispers in the dreams of princes
stages.clues: Rulers dream of a serpent that promises power; a governor grows greedy for conquest past all reason; the Shansabani heir is seen among the khan's advisers.
stages.ignored: The demon chooses his host.
stages.stopped: The dreamer is warned, or purified at a fire temple.
stages.turned: The troupe sets a trap for the demon in the dreamer.

stages.title: A new Zahhak
stages.clues: A ruler hides his shoulders; people vanish near his palace; he learns sorcery overnight.
stages.ignored: The Zahhak turns to evil and is taught the dark arts, drawing power from other demons.
stages.stopped: The possession is broken while the host still resists, before he embraces evil.
stages.turned: The host fights the demon from within, with the troupe's help.

stages.title: The serpent's reign
stages.clues: Virtue is mocked at court and cruelty rewarded.
stages.ignored: Persia falls under a tyrant like the first Zahhak, and her sahirs must rise against him.
stages.stopped: A hero, perhaps Rostam roused, brings the Zahhak down.

links.note: Zahhak's line; an heir at court
Guard a rite against Persia's foes

neighbours.secrets: The book leaves it to the troupe whether the demon is behind the Mongols. If he is, ridding the horde of him can be a whole saga; if not, he waits for another ruler's ambition.

neighbours.name: The Demons of Ghur and Kabul
neighbours.summary:
Driven by the familiar demons and evil spirits the Shansabani abandoned when the Khwarazm-shah drove them out of Ghur. Malicious jinn haunt its roads, demons in human shape live in its towns, and in some of them they now rule openly while the Ghurs watch even their own families for signs of a stranger behind familiar eyes. No one has replaced the Shansabani as lords of the province.

To the east, Kabul answers to a demon its people call only the Shadowed One, unseen even by his subjects, through four lieutenants with demon-given powers; his hold is tied to the trade in myrobalan, whose addicts fill the markets. Ghazni's wealth flows from a False God its people worship in secret.

details.antagonist: The demons the Shansabani left behind, and the Shadowed One

stages.title: The roads close
stages.clues: Caravans through Ghur are lost; myrobalan spreads west through the markets of Khurasan.
stages.ignored: More of Ghur's towns fall to their demons.
stages.stopped: A town is cleansed and its demon driven out.

stages.title: The Shadowed One reaches out
stages.clues: Myrobalan merchants appear in Herat and Nishapur; officials there begin to wear the addicts' stained teeth.
stages.ignored: Kabul's demon has servants in the cities of Persia.
stages.stopped: The trade is broken and the lieutenants unmasked.
stages.turned: The troupe learns the Shadowed One's name, and with it a hold on him.

stages.title: Ghur's demon kingdom
stages.clues: The Mongols' coming leaves the province no human lord at all.
stages.ignored: Ghur becomes a land ruled by demons, a road for Hell into the east.

neighbours.name: Saving Merv's Books
neighbours.summary:
Driven by the sahirs of Merv's house of wisdom, keepers of the grand vizier Nizam al-Mulk's library of magic, who learned from the Ghuzz what an invader does to a city. Merv holds thousands of books that exist nowhere else, in the 'Aziziyah, the Kamaliyah, the Dumayriyah and the college libraries; the colleges and madrasas will not send them away, so the sahirs copy all they can before Genghis Khan comes.

The copying turns up forgotten secrets (the place of Solomon's Seal, perhaps), tempts the sahirs to steal books the clerics keep locked away, and puts the best of Nizam al-Mulk's tomes on the road west, where hostile magicians wait for them.

details.antagonist: The Mongol horde, and those who would profit from the panic

stages.title: The copyists at work
stages.clues: Sahirs buy up paper and ink, hire scribes and borrow books they never return; a copied page names something no one should know.
stages.ignored: A few hundred books are copied in time.
stages.stopped: The troupe helps copy or carry the most precious.
stages.turned: A raid on the Dumayriyah frees a tome of Isma'ili theology, and the Nizaris take an interest.

stages.title: The caravan west
stages.clues: Nizam al-Mulk's chief tomes leave Merv under guard; rival magicians, sahirs or magi, learn the road.
stages.ignored: The caravan is robbed, and its magic changes hands.
stages.stopped: The books reach a safe house in the west.
stages.turned: The troupe's own library is where they come to rest.

stages.title: Merv falls
stages.clues: If history holds, the Mongols come to Khurasan.
stages.ignored: Merv is sacked and its libraries perish; only what was copied or carried away survives.

links.note: Want a tome of their theology

neighbours.name: The Apparition at Durenmar
neighbours.summary:
Driven by whatever has stirred on the Great Steppe, where the Aquila, the lost second apprentice of Hercynius, was last seen riding east in the late eleventh century in search of untouched wilds. As the Mongols lay Transoxiana waste, ripples of its death and ruin reach the Order of Hermes: the Primus of Ex Miscellanea dreams strangely, diviners of several Houses foretell disaster, Tremere's spies hear of a danger in the east, the Tenens of the East frets at the chaos beyond the Levant, and even House Merinita reports new lands and stories stirring in Arcadia.

At the Grand Tribunal of 1228, thirty-three years after the last, something walks through Durenmar's wards.

details.antagonist: The Aquila's lost line, or a shaman walking in spirit

stages.title: Ripples in the West
stages.clues: Prophecies, dreams and Arcadian turbulence trouble the Houses; Tremere puts its intelligence to work.
stages.ignored: The Order argues about the east and does nothing.
stages.turned: The troupe is sent to see what is happening.

stages.title: The third day of the Grand Tribunal
stages.clues: The Aegis stands, but a translucent man with a legionary standard, or an eagle, or both at once, takes shape beside the Praeco.
stages.ignored: Philipus Niger's attack does nothing; the figure looks round in silence and fades. Xavier of Mercere, the old archivist, says it looks like the lost Aquila.
stages.stopped: The spirit is caught or followed home.
stages.turned: The troupe goes east to find the Aquila's heirs before anyone else does.

neighbours.secrets: Whether it is the Aquila himself or a shaman of his line travelling by phantasticum, the book does not say. If his lineage survived on the steppe, two centuries apart from the Order, its magic may no longer look Hermetic, its loyalty may lie with the nomads, and it may have given Parma Magica to the horde's hedge wizards.

neighbours.name: Itineris Serica
neighbours.summary:
Driven by Cartophilius of Mercere, who wants a covenant on the move that will cross Asia to Serica and find the source of silk. Several magi objected that the Order has never had a Seeker covenant of the kind; to everyone's surprise the Exarch of House Tremere backed the plan in full and offered two seasoned Tremere to ride with it. Whether he believes in it or just wants somewhere to send the hot-heads of the Burning Acorn Vexillation, no one is sure.

As companions on the road the book suggests a Trianoma of the Nestorian faith who spies for her House, a Sufi master of House Criamon born among the Turks, and a Merinita of the Levant who knows the jinn. Their way runs through the lands the Mongols are burning.

details.antagonist: Cartophilius of Mercere and the Exarch of Tremere

stages.title: Fitting out the caravan
stages.clues: Cartophilius looks for magi, grogs, camels and silver; the two Tremere arrive with orders of their own.
stages.ignored: The caravan leaves the west without the troupe.
stages.turned: The troupe joins it, or is it.

stages.title: Through the war
stages.clues: Caravanserais stand empty, towns are ash, Mongol scouts ride the roads, and the sahirs watch the foreigners pass.
stages.ignored: The caravan loses beasts and men, and perhaps its Tremere, to the war.
stages.stopped: It reaches Badakhshan intact.

stages.title: The Faerie road
stages.clues: Up the Wakhan the Faerie aura climbs with every day's march, and side paths open into regiones.
stages.ignored: Some of the company stray into Arcadia and stay.
stages.turned: The road leads beyond the Order's maps, toward Serica.

neighbours.name: The Followers of the Circle Return
neighbours.summary:
Driven by younger Hermetic sahirs of Iberia, heirs of the Followers of the Circle who left the Suhhar in the tenth century and joined the Order of Hermes. Their Solomonic magic has faded under the Code, but not the memory of where it came from, and they hate the Christian kingdoms' reconquest of al-Andalus. They may look east to their lost brethren for help or magical weapons against the heirs of Alfonso the Battler and the followers of Flambeau.

If the Order of Suleiman takes a hand in Iberia's wars, peace between the two orders may be out of reach for decades.

stages.title: An Iberian at the Majlis
stages.clues: A sahir from Iberia comes to Baghdad speaking for a community outside the Order of Hermes, reminds the viziers that another crusade threatens Islam in the west, and asks them to restore the old alliance.
stages.ignored: The viziers argue, and some promise help in secret.
stages.stopped: The Majlis refuses him.
stages.turned: The troupe carries word between east and west.

stages.title: Weapons for al-Andalus
stages.clues: Solomonic devices and bound spirits turn up in Iberian battles; House Flambeau notices.
stages.ignored: The Order of Hermes blames the Hermetic sahirs, and Iberia's Tribunal splits.
stages.stopped: The trade is uncovered before blood is shed.

stages.title: Two orders at war
stages.clues: Wizard Wars are declared in Iberia over sahir aid.
stages.ignored: The Suhhar and the Order of Hermes fight in the west as well as the east.
stages.turned: A settlement brings the Iberians home to one order or the other.

characters.name: Niya al-Waziriyya al-Jabr Satefa al-Inshai al-Qasri al-Qalb
characters.summary:
Vizier of the Dar al-Hikma, a Gifted sahira of the Heart. She has found a way of joining her Solomonic arts that gives her two spells of her own: one calls a spirit straight out of the Magic Realm, the other many spirits at once. For that the house chose her to lead it, young as she is and Gifted though she is, and she is likely to be the next Asala al-Qalb when the present one dies.

She holds that the Order has stagnated and that its Gifted members are its best hope of surviving, a view few share: under a tenth of the sahirs are Gifted, and those are not much liked. If Kha'trazh dies between meetings she would act for him by custom, and is unlikely to keep the post at the vote.

characters.name: Meriq al-Asala al-Qalani al-Safar al-Najm
characters.summary:
The Asala al-Najm, head of the Followers of the Star, a wizened old man of Savah best known for a hat that seems to be on inside out; his head, he jokes, sits on his hat. When the last Asala vanished from Nasibin in 1186 Meriq put himself forward, and the astrologer-viziers, having asked the stars, accepted him. Many now think he takes the charge too lightly, but no one asks him to go.

He is unGifted, a fine communicator, and the author of many good books on Artes Liberales, Solomonic Astrology and more. He maintains that the House of the Heavens at Nasibin is still the family's home.

characters.name: Nil al-Wazir al-Salih al-Yad
characters.summary: Vizier of the House of Healing at Gundeshapur, a Follower of the Hand born to a Christian family, who took Islam after he joined the Order. He is a great historian of the Middle East and knows Europe's past as well. He is no great healer, to his family's disappointment, and prefers Solomonic Storytelling; his singing voice is said to enchant. The accusations made against him at the Majlis do not seem to trouble him.
characters.secrets: Many believe he is far too close to the Nizaris, some of whom have called on him at the House of Healing; how close, the book does not say.

characters.name: 'Arkhaman Laqy al-Hayz al-Nahr

tradition_effects.name: Kharrat, the braggart
tradition_effects.parameters: Summons Kharrat (Infernal Might 10) by his name.

tradition_effects.name: What are the words that surround [Target]?
tradition_effects.parameters: Detail: Thorough, Ritual. While his spirit keeps it up he hears everything spoken near the target, without being there.

tradition_effects.name: [Spirit], his arms wide
tradition_effects.parameters: Allure: Simple. Listeners grasp a brief message carried in his voice, whatever their language.

tradition_effects.name: Make their eyelids heavy and their heads to fall
tradition_effects.parameters: Allure: Supernatural. Everyone in earshot falls into a natural sleep; supernatural perception may resist.

tradition_effects.name: Through the gray haze
tradition_effects.parameters: Delay: Sun. At dawn or dusk opens a way through a regio boundary of up to the spell's magnitude + 3.

tradition_effects.name: [Spirit] brings the curse of Bayna
tradition_effects.parameters: Delay: Immediate. A target he touches gains two Warping Points.

tradition_effects.name: We will meet again as the seasons turn
tradition_effects.parameters: Delay: Season, Ritual. Draws a portal from one supernatural aura to another of the same realm he has been to; sahirs use it to reach the Majlis.

bound_beings.name: Kharrat
bound_beings.notes: His Infernal Spirit Companion, whom he believes his father; held so far with vis.

description.biography: His Sihr is of the Magic realm. Solomonic Travel 10 is +2 with his Puissant Virtue (10+2 in the book).

characters.summary:
A young sahir of the River, vizier of the house at Sana'a. His mother, niece of the imam, bore him in secret at the house to keep him from her uncle, and said his father was a black-eyed jinni of flame. Raised by the sahirs, he wanted only to serve them, and as he grew to look like his mother's family they brought him into the Order. The first spirit he summoned was Kharrat, the Infernal jinni he believes to be that father, whom he has kept in hand with vis so far.

His Gift came late, and its power has made him wild: one spell leads him to cast another, and his taint unsettles those without The Gift. His masters fear he will go mad without Gifted company, so they have made him vizier and are sending him to Baghdad this summer. He is pale, with black hair, thin brows and a curled moustache, an innocent twinkle and a confident smile, a hooded robe that has hardly travelled, and usually a seat.
characters.secrets: Kharrat is sure that the boy's longing for a father's approval will carry him into evil, and means to bind him to a duty to go and find his mother, whose shame the spirit would relish.

characters.name: Kha'trazh al-Wazir al-Dall Ariq al-Qalb
characters.summary:
Grand vizier of the Order of Suleiman for nearly thirty years, a Follower of the Heart from Basra. He is calm and quiet and weighs every word; no one thinks him especially clever or strong, and he lacks The Gift. He took the laqab al-Wazir al-Dall, 'the dignified vizier', as a promise not to abuse his place. The viziers keep electing him because he heeds them, hears out anyone who wants to speak, and stays on fair terms with all five Asalat. Close to a hundred years old, he looks barely fifty, and many expect him to die soon.

He avoids open conflict with the Order of Hermes for now. At the Majlis he holds formal council the first evening, into the night and all the next day, keeping the hardest matters for the second evening after dinner, and does not mind who dozes.

Story seeds:
A Test of Arms: the Followers of the Stone choose their Asala by combat, and a vengeful sahir who hates Kha'trazh may challenge his own family's head to win the seat and a vote against him.
The Vizier's Opposition: Kha'trazh expels a well-loved sahir accused of betraying the Suhhar, and the leader of his opponents promises to bring the exile back in exchange for votes.

characters.name: Cartophilius
characters.summary: A magus of Mercere thought odd even by his own House's lights, son of Geographicus, who helped found an earlier covenant that travelled. At the last Normandy Tribunal he proposed another: a band of magi passing as a merchant caravan, going east to fabled Serica to find where silk truly comes from, and asking to be funded as a covenant devoted to research. He belongs to no covenant yet.
