creatures.name: Al-Khidr, the Green One
creatures.appearance: An old Muslim in a woollen cloak, his skin and clothes tinged blue-green by the Water of Life.
creatures.notes:
A prophet of Islam who cannot die, having drunk of the Water of Life, which he reached by the light of a jewel Adam brought from Paradise; in some tales he and Alexander sought it together, and Alexander lost his way in the dark. He roams the world advising where God sends him, and is said to have guided every prophet since his birth save Muhammad, who taught him instead. Sky, sea and every growing thing obey him, and the Sufis hold him the perfect shaykh.

The sahirs say he taught Solomon his secrets, and the Nizaris count him among the forms of their immortal imam. He taught Nur al-Din magic before the Order of Suleiman's guide could, and their talk is kept in a book at Baghdad. He rarely gives his name, and his advice can seem mad but always proves right; he helps those who seek the Water of Life only if they mean well. Shamakhi's Rock of Moses marks where Moses met him.

Named without stats: neither book gives his Might or powers.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 137

creatures.name: Kharrat the Braggart
creatures.weakness: Protected Group: a victim who rejects him wholly and willingly, spending a Confidence Point on it; and anyone who speaks the Bismillah.

powers.name: Apparition
powers.description: Takes an illusory shape that only his chosen victim, 'Arkhaman, can see; to him it seems a living person in every way.

powers.name: Protection of the Close Friend
powers.description: His chosen victim cannot move against him unless sorely provoked, as a son could not strike his mother. The victim may rage at him freely, but each fresh attempt to oppose him in deed takes a great effort of will.

powers.name: Control Human
powers.description: If it penetrates, he commands his companion, who obeys as well as he can; the victim may try to throw off the control each time he is told to act against his faith. Its Initiative is his Quickness.

powers.name: Envisioning
powers.description: Enters his companion's dreams for 1 point, slowly darkening them and speaking through any figure in them; or, for 5 points, forces a waking vision of whatever he likes. A vision can stun for a round, and the victim needs a Brave roll of 9+ to avoid retching, fits or terror. The text gives the cost once as 1 or 2; the pack follows the power's own account and the qareen's (1 or 5).

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Forms a body, as Realms of Power: The Infernal p. 31 describes.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Stirs the trait Overconfident in a victim, for 1 to 3 points, as Realms of Power: The Infernal p. 31 describes.

creatures.appearance: A pale man whose eyes are wholly black and smoke like embers. Most of the time he stays in spirit form, unseen.
creatures.notes: A vain, haughty shaitan whom the young sahir 'Arkhaman of Sana'a summoned as his first spirit, believing him to be his father. Kharrat thinks the boy is wholly his and that the longing to please a father will lead him into evil. So far 'Arkhaman has kept him in hand with vis, as his elders warned him to. Reputations: none.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 35
creatures.secrets: His aim is to bind 'Arkhaman by an accepted duty and send him to find his mother, the imam's niece who hid his birth: the shame his coming would bring her is what the demon relishes.

creatures.name: The Buran of Yenghissar
creatures.weakness: Protected Group: anyone who speaks the Bismillah.

powers.name: Delusion of the Desert
powers.description: Shows a lost traveller his missing friends or a welcoming oasis before it falls on him, or shows itself as a sandstorm in a man's shape with burning eyes to terrify. An image of one thing costs 1 point, one filling a room 5. Every such image has some flaw: a wrong smell, or only one person sees it.

powers.name: Elemental Control of Wind
powers.description: Any Creo, Muto or Rego Auram effect, at 1 Might point a magnitude (so its cost varies), up to a level no higher than its Might and never a Ritual.

powers.name: Recalcitrance
powers.description: Always active. Any supernatural attempt to control it, though not to destroy it, treats its Might as half again as high, or raises the Ease Factor by half: a Circular Ward Against Demons must be of level 38 to hold it back.

vis.where: vis prava, left as black sand when it is dispersed

creatures.appearance: A huge formless whirl of raging black sand; Second Sight makes out a giant shadow in a man's shape inside it.
creatures.notes:
A wild storm spirit of the desert that once fell on the village of Yenghissar, on the road to Khashgar, every seventh year, ruining its crops and herds. A careless sahir of Infernal bent has bound it into his family's sword with the Goetic Art of Binding (Realms of Power: The Infernal p. 117), and it rages to be free, stirring up the elements around him. It is mute: its Arabic is how much it understands.

It has no body and cannot touch the world but by its powers, so it has no combat, Soak or wounds, and lacks the Coagulation and Obsession most demons have. Storm spirits like it haunt the Taklamakan, weaker and stronger; a Magic one is much the same without Recalcitrance or the malice.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 70

creatures.name: Ghul (Infernal)
creatures.how_many: solitary, in graveyards, refuse pits and slums; Might usually no more than 20
creatures.weakness: Protected Group: anyone who speaks the Bismillah; Vulnerability (iron).

powers.name: Berserker Rage
powers.description: Gives someone, most often itself or its beasts, the Berserk Virtue until they calm down.

powers.name: Change Form
powers.description: Reshapes its own flesh at will into a human or animal form (Corpus or Animal), most ghuls into one kind only, within the natural Size of that kind. It is no spell, so Magic Resistance does nothing against a changed ghul's blows.

powers.name: Endurance of the Enraged
powers.description: Wound penalties do not touch it, except on Defense.

powers.name: Restoration
powers.description: The next blow that strikes it heals, instead, the wound it took the last time it was hurt; one blow each use.

creatures.appearance: A tall, stooped, wild thing with long arms and iron claws, in rags and torn robes filthy with marrow, blood and grave dirt. Cleverer ones look nearly human, but sharp-featured, with pointed or saw-edged teeth and long hooked nails.
creatures.notes:
A degenerate jinni of a debased tribe given to the Infernal, a cannibal of the night that preys on the weak or eats carrion. It goes in heavy robes as a lost traveller, a woman in need or a kindly dervish, and every ghul can take the shape of at least one local scavenger: dog, hyena, jackal or vulture. It scorns weapons for nails and teeth. Folk say a ghul wounded but not slain at one stroke is healed by a second, so lone travellers fear them.

A guide rather than a full block: no Characteristics or combat are printed, and other Abilities differ from ghul to ghul. A true terrestrial demon of the Furies, it cannot become incorporeal and has no Coagulation; this one lacks Envisioning and Obsession too. Exceptional ghuls command rock or flesh, illusions, possession or human magics, and the most feared summon other jinn by Sihr, the Arts Fabulosa or the Goetic Arts. It is not the female faerie ghula, whatever the two share. Its Form, Corpus, is from the book's errata.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 73

creatures.name: Qareen
creatures.how_many: one for each person, as the hadith says; this is a typical one
creatures.weakness: Protected Group: a victim who rejects it wholly and willingly, spending a Faith Point on it; and the jinn's usual weaknesses.

powers.name: Apparition
powers.description: Takes an illusory shape only its companion sees, who takes it for a real person.

powers.name: Control Human
powers.description: If it penetrates, the qareen commands its companion, who may fight free each time an order goes against his faith.

powers.name: Envisioning
powers.description: Haunts its companion's dreams for 1 point, twisting them darker little by little and speaking through any figure in them; or, for 5 points, forces a waking vision that can stun him for a round, after which a Brave roll of 9+ is needed to keep from retching, fits or terror. Its favourite way of speaking to him.

powers.name: Protection of the Appointed Companion
powers.description: Its companion can no more move against it than against his own mother: he may be furious with it, but to oppose it in deed takes great will and a Confidence point, each time.

creatures.appearance: An incorporeal spirit, a wan reflection of its companion to anyone with Second Sight; to the companion it looks lovely or dreadful as its schemes require.
creatures.notes:
The companion spirit Islamic tradition gives every person, a private tempter. This block is for a person burdened with Plagued by a Supernatural Entity (Qareen), a Major Story Flaw, who sees and knows his qareen; quieter ones, behind the Impious Friend or Manufactured Ignorance Flaws, have a Might of 5 to 10. Its whispers seem to come from the victim's own mind, and the storyguide gives them as advice, never naming a demon.

Strength, Stamina and Dexterity are n/a (it has no body, and no Coagulation); the Communication printed has no label and is taken as +3. Its Abilities vary: up to 300 experience points' worth, often matching its companion's, used to help or hinder him.

Story seeds:
A Pious Companion?: a character of rare piety may persuade a dark Faerie qareen to submit to Islam and become a guardian, easy to mistake for an angel; an Infernal qareen is a true demon and can never be redeemed.
An Unwanted Guest: a magus newly come to the east finds a Faerie qareen has attached itself to him, unbeliever though he is; mastering it is reason enough for the Suhhar, and an open-minded group of sahirs sends him a courteous invitation to join.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 74

creatures.name: Azi Dahak, Duke of the Spirits of Deceit
creatures.order: Duke of the Spirits of Deceit
creatures.weakness: Abhorrent Material: flame from a Mazdean fire temple.

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Forms a body, and lets it go when he likes.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: Stirs the trait Power Hungry, for 1 to 3 points (Realms of Power: The Infernal p. 31).

powers.name: Envisioning
powers.description: Appears in someone's dreams.

powers.name: Possession
powers.description: Costs what he puts into it, and he usually puts in his whole Might Pool, ruling his victim's acts. He regains no Might while he possesses, so he must leave now and then; meanwhile the victim dreams of his own death and damnation and may try to bar the demon's return (Realms of Power: The Infernal p. 32).

powers.name: Trust of the Innocent
powers.description: The target believes one plausible lie until shown otherwise; Intelligence against 6 resists.

powers.name: Forked Tongue of the Serpent
powers.description: The target believes any lie, however absurd, until he repeats it to someone and hears how foolish it is. An Intelligence roll of 9+ also sees through it, the first an hour after and then once an hour.

powers.name: The Serpent's Oracle
powers.description: Works any Intellego effect, or foresees the nearest consequences of one chosen act.

powers.name: Empower the Possessed
powers.description: A victim he possesses who wilfully uses a Goetic Art adds Azi Dahak's own score in it, and may use the demon's Hierarchy in place of his own.

creatures.appearance: Seldom seen in the flesh: a vast winged serpent with three heads, each with two eyes and three pairs of fangs. Snakes and scorpions pour from his wounds. He bites three foes a round, acting as a Trained Group of three.
creatures.notes:
The demon whose host becomes Zahhak. The first Zahhak, the tyrant of Persia's heroic age, ruled a thousand years from Ctesiphon after sawing Jamshid in half, until Feridun ended his reign; since then a Zahhak has risen from time to time and Persian sahirs have fought him, never again so mighty. The last was the Shansabani sultan Muhammad of Ghur, beaten fourteen years ago. A possessed man grows a black snake from each shoulder that grows back when cut and hungers for human brains; only ending the possession cures it.

At first the demon makes his host do evil, and slowly his promises corrupt the host himself; none has yet held out. Once the host embraces evil the demon teaches him the Goetic Arts, Ablating above all, to lengthen his life, gain Magic Resistance and steal the powers of other spirits. His Goetic Arts are entered as Abilities.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 143
creatures.secrets: Some Persian sahirs suspect that Genghis Khan is a Zahhak, or takes counsel from one, since he turns on Persia the way Azi Dahak's hosts do; whether it is so is the storyguide's choice. The first Zahhak was never slain: an angel helped Feridun chain him beneath Mount Damavand, where he lives yet, freed of the demon and kept from death by holy bonds.

creatures.name: Jumayl, a Jinni Guide

powers.name: Cuirass of the Zephyr
powers.description: As Circling Winds of Protection, lasting for as long as he goes on reciting verses of the Qur'an (the Duration of Recitation, much like Concentration).

powers.name: Blinding Light of the Pious
powers.description: As Flash of the Scarlet Flames.

powers.name: Tay al-Ard (Travel)
powers.description: Takes him, and two people whose hands he holds, at once to any place he has visited or holds an Arcane Connection to, however far. As the Leap of Homecoming at Touch and Group; one Intricacy point lowers its cost.

creatures.equipment: A fine Damascus steel long sword, a caravan guard's leather scale armour, showy jewellery.
creatures.appearance: A handsome, supple man of no clear Eastern people, with skin like alabaster and white hair, one eye an iridescent green and the other the blue of the sea. He wears swirling robes of deep blue over light leather, set off with gold. His name means little camel.
creatures.notes:
One of the jann: a mercenary guide condemned, for a crime his brother did, to wander the caravanserais of the trade routes from the Levant to Transoxiana and further. A fine swordsman and woodsman, he is known to Muslim merchants and even the Levant's Redcaps for his good humour and his daring against raiders. Any great city of the region may hold him, but he likes best the markets by the fortress of al-Mushaqqar in Bahrayn, for the well-paid work and the cheap drink. Like most faerie jinn he can take a beast's shape, in his case a white wild Bactrian camel (Skinchanger). Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses.

He never tires, yet ordinary wine undoes him easily. Spent Might comes back only after a full night's rest and a meal among fellow travellers in a human settlement, with their rations or an inn's food, drink men have brewed, and their songs and tales of the road: each eight hours restores Might equal to the aura, as adjusted for his realm, or 1 at least. He need not truly eat. He guards his True Name and leaves no Arcane Connections about. Made as a magus-level character by Realms of Power: Faerie; to make him a plain companion, drop Ostentatious, Highly Cognizant and the two Increased Might Virtues, make his powers Lesser, and trade his Might Recovery Flaw for three Minor Flaws.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 64

creatures.name: Bali' al-Ard, the Swallower of the Ground

powers.name: Drinker of the Wind
powers.description: Carries him at once to any place within seven leagues that he can see or holds an Arcane Connection to. As Seven League Stride, but not being Hermetic it takes his rider too. Four Intricacy points speed it and cheapen it.

powers.name: Immateriality
powers.description: Makes him immaterial until the next sunrise or nightfall.

creatures.equipment: Tack and harness of rare quality, horseshoes of coppery gold.
creatures.appearance: A splendid Arabian stallion, of the breed famed even in Europe.
creatures.notes:
The jinni racehorse of a young Bedouin sahir, Salih al-Kamil, who loves him dearly. (The text calls the example horse Hesaan, which only means horse; the block names him Bali' al-Ard, and the pack does too.) He never tires and can travel by magic, so in the dust and muddle of a long desert race he cheats, winning his master glory that feeds the horse's need for vitality. Breeders hound the sahir to put mares to him, not knowing that stud work takes the horse from his master's side and can never get a foal. He can take no shape but a horse's, though he can become immaterial.

His Quickness specialty is racing (Mythic Quickness, allowed though Heroic, since it makes the racehorse); like any horse he has +3 to running. He is a fit khadim, a servant spirit, for a new unGifted sahir with small Solomonic scores; built on a courser and not balanced as a player's character. Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 65

creatures.name: 'Abd al-Qininna, Servant of the Bottle

powers.name: Binding Oath
powers.description: A Ritual Power. Whoever frees the seemingly captive 'afrit may bargain for three wishes, or for a span of conditional service as its nature dictates, if he swears to destroy the bottle and set the jinni free for ever. Five Intricacy points cheapen it.

powers.name: Eidolon
powers.description: Taken twice: its glamour shows both as the copper bottle that seems to hold it and as a towering column of smoke in a man's shape rising from the bottle's mouth.

powers.name: Illusionary Home
powers.description: Raises a sumptuous phantom palace for whoever holds the bottle.

powers.name: Flight
powers.description: Always active: as Wings of the Soaring Wind.

powers.name: Loosely Material
powers.description: At a cost that varies, gives a would-be master a plain bottle to handle, or gives its 'afrit form enough substance to carry loads, use Touch powers or fight when its master bids.

powers.name: Tay al-Ard (Travel)
powers.description: Bears the 'afrit and whatever it carries at once to any place the bottle's holder has visited or holds an Arcane Connection to, at any distance; as the Leap of Homecoming. One Intricacy point cheapens it.

powers.name: Serendipitous Wealth
powers.description: A Ritual Power that seems to grant the Wealthy Virtue, but, like the False Gods' Wealth of Nations, fetches the treasure from somewhere else (Realms of Power: The Infernal p. 37). Five Intricacy points cheapen it.

creatures.appearance: At first a solid copper flask shaped like a gourd, stoppered with lead stamped with Suleiman's seal. Disturb the seal and it becomes a pillar of smoke topped by a vast torso, red or sometimes blue or green, with a monstrous horned or jag-toothed face. The novice takes that for the faerie; the jinni is still a bodiless spirit under the glamour.
creatures.notes:
One of the Bottles of Suleiman, a kind of faerie jinni grown from the folk tales of poor fishermen who net a sealed copper flask, a cucurbite, and free a grateful or furious jinni from it. These jinn take the shape of the bottle itself and play out stories of riches and humbling (Realms of Power: Faerie p. 79) on any shore of the Islamic lands, near fishing villages. This one is servile. Its External Vis is the copper bottle, which grants Self-Confident. Intelligence is n/a as printed (taken as 0); no combat is printed. Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses.

Too strong and too tied to its story to be a player's character; only a very experienced sahir could bind it as a khadim, though weaker bottles might suit younger ones. Drawn from two tales of the Nights, The City of Brass and The Fisherman and the Jinni. It is left unplaced: such bottles wash up anywhere along the coasts.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 66

creatures.name: Ghula (Faerie)
creatures.how_many: in the cities and deserts, each in her chosen household

powers.name: Cause Drowsiness
powers.description: Puts a person she touches to sleep. ReCo (Base 4, +1 Touch, +4 Until); one Intricacy point cheapens it.

powers.name: Illusionary Home
powers.description: Always active: a glamour that makes a place look, sound, smell, feel and even taste like the home her role calls for. MuIm (Base 5, +3 Structure, +2 Sun, +1 Touch, +1 constant); four Intricacy points cheapen it.

powers.name: Transform Into Human
powers.description: A Personal Power that turns her between her human shape and her feeding shape. MuCo(An) (Base 10, +2 Sun, +1 Size); five Intricacy points cheapen it and speed it.

creatures.appearance: Usually a beautiful woman posing as a rich widow or an orphan of good family who needs a husband, often one driven from her home by war, which makes the tale ring true. The eyes and the inside of the mouth of an Arab ghula are always green.
creatures.notes:
A dark faerie jinniyya of the desert, risen from, or wearing the face of, those who die of thirst there. She weds a strong, rich man and drinks his blood as he sleeps; with vitality enough she bears a child that looks like its father but is a ghula too, born with teeth. By night the ghulas of a city slip out to feast and drain the dead in the graveyards. In the usual tale the husband finds them out and destroys the nest but spares his child, who grows up to lord it over the city and drive him out; the broken old man then haunts the outskirts warning travellers of his part in the ruin, and his telling feeds the ghuls' fame. Another tale makes them the ghosts of harlots given flesh, who lure weak-willed men to lonely places, put them to sleep and crush their heads with stones. Male faerie ghuls exist but only serve the ghulas.

Restricted in daylight; locked into a body though a spirit; not meant as a player's character. First given in Realms of Power: Faerie p. 72; this one is the Arab jinniyya, not the European lamia. The book prints her Might with no Form; its errata give Corpus. Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 72

creatures.name: Baghl, the Earth Jinni

powers.name: Flesh to Stone
powers.description: Turns a person he touches to stone until sunrise or the dawn call to prayer (Base 20, +1 Touch, +2 Sun); three Mastery points cheapen it.

powers.name: Ruler of Earth
powers.description: His Focus Power: any non-Ritual Perdo or Rego Terram effect up to level 15, at 1 Might point a magnitude (1 to 3).

powers.name: Incorporeal
powers.description: Always active: by nature unseen and untouchable, beyond the reach of the physical world. Magic can aim at him only if the caster can sense him. In this state he has no physical scores, and uses his physical Characteristics only against other bodiless beings.

powers.name: Donning the Corporeal Veil
powers.description: Makes the body described under Appearance, with its arms and armour, its Size, combat scores and wounds. It never tires and lasts until he lets it go; killing it does not kill him.

powers.name: Presence
powers.description: Always active: he knows everything that happens in his haunt. It must penetrate to sense anyone with Magic Resistance.

vis.where: in his body, if he is slain in the flesh

creatures.appearance: A fat man with a mule's head, eyes like pupilless jet and limbs seamed with quartz, swinging a huge maul. In the flesh he can also take the shape of a big black mule.
creatures.notes: The jinni of a dark cave in the Elburz mountains, quarried once until he drove the miners away. Leaving him to admire his fine rock formations mostly keeps him calm, and now and then he will talk with scholars of theology. He knows Islam fairly well and may feign the faerie jinn's weakness to folk rites, though only the muezzin's call truly harms him. His haunt is an Arcane Connection to him (+1 to the Penetration multiplier); better ones come only from his body. His cave gives 1 pawn of Terram vis a year, a quartz-crusted stalactite at its back (the cave's vis, not his).
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 69

creatures.name: Zawba'a, Whirlwind of the Desert
creatures.how_many: one whirlwind to a stretch of desert

powers.name: Donning the Corporeal Veil
powers.description: Takes a body (Size +1) so it can strike foes; a Greater Power (Realms of Power: Magic p. 102).

powers.name: Flay
powers.description: Its touch tears the skin half off a foe, who takes a Heavy Wound. A Greater Power, its Mastery points spent on cost, speed and Penetration.

powers.name: Presence
powers.description: Always active: it knows all that passes in its haunt, which may be as large as a Structure (Realms of Power: Magic p. 103).

vis.where: in the little whirl of black sand it leaves
in the little whirl of black sand it leaves

creatures.appearance: In the flesh, a pillar of sand some eight feet tall spinning fast, with a spiteful, bloodthirsty face chuckling at its heart.
creatures.notes:
A jinni of the Arabian sands that loves to kill whoever crosses its path. It knows only the head-on charge, so it is easily outwitted. Its Bloodthirsty trait is Essential and is counted in its attack; Flay adds to the harm. Some seasoned sahirs strike bargains with zawba'a and bind them as khadims, riding them across the land as whirling sandstorms, a sight that awes even great princes.

Story seeds:
Death by Zawba'a?: a man is found flayed in a room dusted with fine sand; the trail leads to a secret circle of sahirs from a minor sect who have learned to bind the whirlwind jinn and loose them on their political enemies.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 103

creatures.name: Ighraq al-Siq, the Drowning Flood of the Gorge

params.power: Grant Wilding, only to those with Water Lore

powers.name: Crafter of Water
powers.description: His Focus Power: any non-Ritual Creo or Rego Aquam effect up to level 40, at 1 Might point a magnitude (1 to 8). He may use a Range of the waterway (as Sight) and a Target of the body of water (as Structure), reaching anyone on or in his reach of the river, or the whole Zab (Realms of Power: Magic p. 43). Three Mastery points raise its level by 15.

powers.name: Drown
powers.description: In floodwave form only: after a melee blow lands he swallows a foe smaller than himself, who must roll against deprivation (ArM5 pp. 180-181) and may struggle free each round by the grappling rules (ArM5 p. 174).

powers.name: Donning the Corporeal Veil
powers.description: Takes the body under Appearance, with its arms, armour, combat scores and wounds; it never tires and lasts until he lets it go, and killing it does not kill him. Slow: it needs an extra round to prepare.

powers.name: Grant Water Lore
powers.description: Gives someone the Minor Mystery Virtue Water Lore, for a while or for good (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp. 103-104). His canyon is a source of Quality 4; a magus who talks the spiteful jinni into teaching him learns as from a teacher, at Quality 9.

powers.name: Grant Wilding
powers.description: Gives the Major Mystery Virtue Wilding to someone who already has a Water Lore score, for a while or for good (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp. 105-106).

powers.name: Presence
powers.description: Always active once he is loose: he knows all that happens in his haunt; it must penetrate to sense anyone with Magic Resistance.

powers.name: Transform into Floodwave
powers.description: Becomes a flood that seems to draw on the river's own water. Slow: it needs an extra round to prepare.

vis.where: in smooth stones of many hues, if he is slain

creatures.appearance: A lean giant with blue-green skin and lank green-black hair like river weed, bearing a great spear and a vest of water-worn stones. Once manifest he can break into his favourite shape, a flood full of hurtling stones that runs up or down the watercourse. A Deluge of Rushing and Dashing in that narrow gorge is terrible.
creatures.notes:
An old pagan spirit of the Tigris, once free along its length and now held to one stretch of the Lesser Zab, the Siq al-Majnun or Jinni's Gorge, where his spring floods burst through the narrow canyon (a Magic aura of 6). He shrinks from even setting foot on the banks. He is sealed in a carved stone block at the gorge, as some lost cities' gates are guarded: while sealed he can do nothing and is hidden in the native rock, which takes his Magic Resistance; the ground about it is an Arcane Connection to him (+1 to the Penetration multiplier, +3 to someone touching the block barefoot). His gorge gives 2 pawns of Aquam a year, rainwater gathering in a niche of that block (the gorge's vis).

Built as an Autumn character by Realms of Power: Magic, from a base Might of 35 raised to 40 by Improved Might, and not meant to be balanced. He has a True Name like any jinni but no Daimon Virtue. His Flood trait is Essential; Water Lore is his Nature Lore Virtue. The block gives his Might no Form: the pack takes Aquam. A Faerie or Infernal version, or one of Auram or Terram with a Might of 20 to 25, can be made from him.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 130

creatures.name: Nisnas
creatures.how_many: many, in the forests of Yemen and Hadramawt

powers.name: Hop like the Wind
powers.description: Huge bounds that carry it swiftly over the ground, like the Gift of the Frog's Legs but with a great leap every round. A Greater Power, cheapened and speeded.

creatures.appearance: A small man split down the middle: a faceless half head, one side of a body with a single arm and leg, a sheep's tail, and half a face sunk into its chest.
creatures.notes:
A shy, harmless wild thing that seems to come from Hadramawt, whose people find its flesh sweet and hunt it for the pot; its Enemies Flaw is theirs. It can talk, and stories tell of nisnases who pleaded for their lives before they were killed. Its curiosity is a Compulsion; Fast (Leaping) is its Essential Trait.

Story seeds:
An Escaped Nisnas: a fleeing nisnas begs the characters to save it from the people who mean to eat it; it is half a man, but has it a soul?
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 116

creatures.name: Giant of 'Ad
creatures.how_many: a people, in regiones deep in the deserts of 'Uman

powers.name: Stonesmith
powers.description: His Focus Power: any non-Ritual Creo, Intellego or Muto Terram effect on stone up to level 20, at 1 Might point a magnitude (1 to 4).

creatures.equipment: Mason's tools, Bedouin robes the colour of sand.
creatures.appearance: Over thirty feet tall, yet far more civilised than Europe's rough giants. Giants of 'Ad love falcons and other hawks, and one usually nests in a giant's long hair or beard.
creatures.notes:
The giants of southern Arabia, of the line of great 'Ad and of Noah's third son: huge magical beings older than Islam who have kept to Magic regiones in the deep desert since they lost their masterpiece, the City of a Thousand Pillars. They are not deathless, and weaken if they stay long away from strong desert Magic auras (Anchored to the Desert). Now and then one comes out to sell his building craft to sorcerers and emirs, asking in return for hints of how to live for ever.

Balanced as a powerful starting companion: 295 experience points for Abilities and 5 free Virtue points, matched by 5 of Flaws. His falcon (his Animal Companion) may be mundane or magical, scaled up as far as Size +3.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 119

creatures.name: Aladlammu and Apsasu
creatures.how_many: a pair: the male aladlammu and the female apsasu

powers.name: Burn the Filthy Spirit
powers.description: Meeting a demon's eye, by sight or Second Sight, strips it of 15 Might. PeVi (Base 5, +1 Eye); a Lesser Power, cheapened and speeded.

powers.name: Repel the Nightstalking Spirit
powers.description: Makes a room or a patch of clear ground safe: if the power penetrates, no demon of Infernal Might 25 or less can enter. Where no boundary exists the beast must mark an unbroken line, which need not be a circle. ReVi (Base 25, +1 for the unusual Target); a Greater Power, cheapened, with 10 experience points of Penetration.

powers.name: Restoration of the Defiled Body
powers.description: As the spell of that name (ArM5 p. 129). A Ritual Power, so it costs a permanent point of Might Score as well as Might points. CrCo (Base 20, +1 Touch), with 15 experience points of Penetration.

creatures.appearance: A mighty bull with vast wings and a bearded man's head; the apsasu has a woman's head. Sparks fly when their hooves strike a foe.
creatures.notes: Guardians made by the old gods, male and female, sworn enemies of harmful spirits and above all the galla, the disease demons that plague them (their Supernatural Nuisance). The same beings with winged human bodies to match their heads are the shedu (male) and lamassu (female). Huge statues of them stand in many great ruins, and a district lucky enough to have one can call on the faerie when disease or demons strike. Someone with the right Area Lore and Faerie Lore can make the amulet that is their Sovereign Ward (Realms of Power: Faerie p. 52). Not meant as player characters. Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 120

creatures.name: Girtablullu, the Scorpion-Man
creatures.how_many: small bands, each a Trained Group, at old ruins

powers.name: Venom
powers.description: The tail's sting: anyone struck needs a Stamina roll of 9+ or takes a Heavy Wound. The sting is a weapon, so the power has no Initiative of its own. PeCo (Base 15, +1 Touch); a Lesser Power, cheapened, with 10 experience points of Penetration.

creatures.equipment: A bow with eleven arrows in the quiver; lamellar armour, as full metal-reinforced leather.
creatures.appearance: A warrior above the waist, long-haired, with a plaited beard; below, the glossy black shell of a scorpion with its long, stinging tail, standing on two clawed legs like a bird's. It carries a bow. Some have wings like a bird's.
creatures.notes: One of the eleven monster-races Tiamat bore to destroy the young gods, taken into the gods' service after Marduk slew her. The gods made the scorpion-men guardians of monuments and holy places, and they belong above all to Shamash the sun god, so explorers of old ruins meet them. Their totals include +3 from Ways of the Desert; Fiercely Protective is an Essential Trait. They are strongest by day: at night they suffer Poor Eyesight, No Sense of Direction and Clumsy (their Greater Malediction).
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 122

creatures.name: Mushhushshu, the Snake-Dragon

powers.name: Assessing Gaze
powers.description: Picks out which of a band of people threatens it most, usually the best fighter; it also notices that magic is present, though not how strong. InCo(Vi) (Base 5, +1 Eye, +2 Group, +1 requisite); a Lesser Power, cheapened and speeded.

powers.name: Voice of Regal Authority
powers.description: Always active: whoever hears its voice feels a strong urge to do as it says. ReMe (Base 5, +2 Sun, +3 Sound, +1 constant); a Greater Power, cheapened.

powers.name: Eye of the Serpent
powers.description: Holds a person rooted by a look. ReCo (Base 5, +1 Eye, +1 Concentration); a Lesser Power, cheapened and speeded.

creatures.appearance: A long snake's body on four legs like a dragon's, the front pair a lion's and the hind pair an eagle's; its head bears horns and a fine crest.
creatures.notes: One of Tiamat's monster-races, given after her death to Ashshur, Assyria's god, whose priests could call and command them; yatus of Harran may still know how. Uncalled, they wander the hills and desert edges of old Assyria from one Magic aura or regio to the next (Desert Regio Network, Realms of Power: Magic p. 45). One will attack armed foreigners within Assyria's old borders, but news or knowledge worth hearing can stay it. Before a fight it uses Assessing Gaze to choose whom to fix with Eye of the Serpent; its sinuous body lets it bite and claw in one round. Brawl 6 gains +2 from Puissant Brawl.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 123

creatures.name: Nasu Spirit
creatures.how_many: a swarm, as large as the corpses it has fed on

powers.name: Donning the Corporeal Veil
powers.description: Takes a body, which it may drop at any time; a nasu seldom leaves the world while there are corpses left to eat. Cr(Re)An (Base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 requisite); a Greater Power, cheapened and speeded.

powers.name: Corpse-Feeding
powers.description: A Ritual Power. A nasu that crawls into an opening of a corpse comes out three rounds later as ten, each its double with this power too, though a swarm of any size holds only one pawn of vis. Every three rounds a swarm can grow by 3 Size, as far as the corpses allow; growing, it attacks the living and makes more corpses. CrAn(Vi) (Base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Group, +1 requisite).

powers.name: Swarm Form
powers.description: A Greater Power with no Hermetic match. A nasu fights only as a swarm, which must be the Size of its foe or more: a hundred thousand (Size +3) can take on an ordinary group of people. Weapons cannot kill it; only area effects such as fire or smoke, each fifth of the swarm caught costing it 1 Might point.

vis.where: in its body (one pawn for a whole swarm)

creatures.appearance: A fly three inches long with a red and yellow striped belly, buzzing horribly in flight.
creatures.notes: A Persian magical spirit, not a jinni, drawn to fresh corpses, most of all those of magical beasts and sorcerers. It seldom takes flesh unless called, and is so slight that any apprentice can call one, which is why masters warn never to: with enough fresh meat, one nasu becomes millions within minutes. Sihr cannot call it, though (Spirit) Summoning can. Its swarm cannot be parried, only dodged (its Defense is n/a, entered as 0). Gluttonous, which the catalog lacks, is left out; Hungry is its Essential Trait. Its wound ranges are 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 or more.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 142

creatures.name: Hyrcanian Tiger
creatures.how_many: lone hunters of Mazandaran and Persia's northern desert

powers.name: Swiftness of Thought
powers.description: It is fast by nature, but for a Might point it covers 500 paces more in one round. ReAn (Base 20, as for ReCo); a Personal Power, cheapened.

creatures.appearance: A long-legged tawny cat some seven feet long with its three-foot tail, weighing about 150 pounds. Mythic Europe's tigers are spotted, not striped, though a saga may have stripes.
creatures.notes:
Named for its arrow-swift running, it lends its name to the Tigris. Persia's old kings kept these tigers as pets, and nobles still pay hunters to steal cubs for training; a pursuing tigress can be fooled with glass balls, taking her reflection for her cub. It eats its prey, mostly gazelle, from its nature though as a magic beast it need not.

It has +3 to every roll for running; Athletics 6 gains +2 from Puissant Athletics, and Swift is an Essential Trait. A Trip that beats the foe's Defense by 3 knocks him down. More than twice as fast as the swiftest horse even unaided, it keeps that pace only a round or two and cannot turn sharply at speed, so prey escapes by dodging and weaving. For a mundane tiger, drop the Might, Magical Qualities, powers and vis; it then tires (Tireless).
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 153

creatures.name: The Simurgh

powers.name: Heart of the Whirlwind
powers.description: Her Focus Power: any non-Ritual effect of the winds up to level 50, at 1 Might point a magnitude (1 to 10); its Initiative is minus its cost.

powers.name: Grant Fertility
powers.description: A Ritual Power worked as she flies over the fields: like The Bountiful Feast, but over ten times the area, and making beasts fruitful as well as crops. CrHe(An) (Base 1, +3 Sight, +4 Year, +4 Boundary, +2 Size, +1 Animal requisite), cheapened by 9 in all.

creatures.appearance: Big enough to carry off an elephant: an eagle with a dog's head and a lion's claws, her feathers the colour of bright-polished copper and her peacock's tail patterned in thirty colours.
creatures.notes:
The vast bird of Mount Damavand, who ranges all over Persia; most Persians have seen her, and her presence strangely reassures them, for she brings fertility and is the pride of the nation. She says she has watched the world destroyed three times, and her long life has made her a sage of many subjects. In her best-known tale she raised the white-haired Zal, Rostam's father, left to die in the Alborz by his own father, and gave him three feathers to summon her when he needed her.

Ordinary weapons barely touch her: only magic weapons or spells wound her. By her External Vis she may give a worthy person one of her breast feathers, holding five pawns of Animal vis; each is an Arcane Connection to her and, thrown into a fire, calls her in great need. Not designed as a player's character. Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 154

creatures.name: Persian Gazelle
creatures.how_many: herds, led by a male
creatures.appearance: A small, delicate antelope with a fawn hide and a dark stripe along each flank; the male's horns are his defence.
creatures.notes: The ghazal, the dorcas of Western bestiaries, common in Persia's Dasht-i Kavir. It sees very keenly (+3 to rolls of sight) and runs fast (+3 to running). Only males have the herd leader's Quality, the large horns and Leadership, and only a male fights; when forced to he gains Ferocity for the while, with 3 temporary Confidence Points.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 155

creatures.name: Olghoi Khorkhoi, the Death Worm
creatures.how_many: lone worms under the northern deserts of Persia and Transoxiana

powers.name: Spit Fire
powers.description: Spits burning venom up to 15 paces on a Thrown Weapon attack, at -2 beyond 5 paces and -4 beyond 10. Only a shield parries it, else it must be dodged with Brawl; a hit does +30 damage. Not usable from June to November (its Restricted Power). CrIg (Base 25, +2 Voice); a Greater Power, cheapened and speeded.

powers.name: Fiery Touch
powers.description: Always active: its burning slime adds +10 damage to its bludgeon and eats metal, so a foe's armour loses a point of Protection even if he soaks it all. CrIg (Base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 corrosive, +1 constant); a Personal Power taken twice, cheapened.

creatures.appearance: A worm five feet long and a foot thick, with no head or tail to be seen, blood-red mottled with black.
creatures.notes:
The grown form of the worm that causes rishtah, which the Ghuzz cure by burying the sick limb in hot sand from dawn to dusk until the worm leaves it; sometimes the worm lives on in the sand and grows to five feet or more, and the Ghuzz say it falls on travellers and herds with fiery venom. It moves freely under the ground and, though blind, feels every tremor. If its Dex + Stealth beats a victim's Per + Awareness it bursts up beside him with +3 to Attack in the first round, before Initiative is rolled. Beasts shy from it by instinct, and horses' alarm is often the first warning.

Its totals include +3 from Ways of the Desert; Stealth 4 gains +2 from Puissant Stealth. Gluttonous, which the catalog lacks, is left out.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 159

creatures.name: Bactrian Camel
creatures.how_many: strings of them in every caravan

powers.name: Smell Water
powers.description: Scents water fit to drink up to two miles off.

powers.name: Survive Without Water
powers.description: Lasts up to two weeks without drinking.

creatures.appearance: The common two-humped riding camel: stubborn, tough and rank, placid most of the year but quick to turn savage in the rutting season. Going weeks without water and finding it underground make it the beast of choice for crossing deserts.
creatures.notes:
The camel of the wider Middle East, beside the one-humped dromedary of North Africa, Egypt, Arabia and the Levant. Wild ones are rare and live only in the far east. Its humour is melancholic with a choleric streak; a few Bjornaer born on Europe's south-eastern edge have a camel heartbeast.

Variants. The pack camel, most of a caravan's: add Domesticated and the Minor Heroic Virtue Great Bearer (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 105: twice the load before it is burdened, and twice the distance before a journey tires it), and drop Survival. The wild camel: add Wilderness Sense and Greater Immunity to thirst, Communication -6, the Defensive Fighter (with its extra Fatigue level), Fast Runner and Herd Animal Qualities, Brawl (dodging) 4 and Wilderness Sense (sense sandstorms) 3; kick Init +0, Atk +5, Dfn +3, Dam +4. The war camel (from a Bactrian or a dromedary): add Aggressive, Pack Animal and Ferocity (when ridden into battle), Brawl (hooves) 5; kick Init +0, Atk +4, Dfn +3, Dam +0; trained, it fights in a Trained Group with its rider.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 170

creatures.name: Asian Elephant
creatures.how_many: a few, kept by nobles or the Khwarazmian army

powers.name: Trunk
powers.description: Always active: the trunk handles things like a hand, though work needing two hands is at -3.

creatures.appearance: The Asian elephant: up to ten feet high and twenty long, weighing as much as 8,000 pounds. This block is the usual tamed cow; only bulls carry tusks worth fighting with.
creatures.notes:
Persia's ancient armies prized war elephants, and a few remain in the east, curiosities for nobles and shock troops for the Khwarazmian army. Elephants are famed foes of dragons and charge serpents without fear, but the squeal of a pig or boar terrifies them (their Fear) and they bolt unless held. They hear superbly and feel tremors through the trunk (+3 to hearing). Each Improved Characteristics gives a Size +4 beast 12 points. Its natural stomp is Init -1, Attack 0, Defense -1, Damage +3, and the trunk only grapples; one dropped from a height on a man does +15 damage. Thick Skin, which the catalog lacks, is left out; Tough Hide is kept.

Variants. The bull: add Aggressive, Extra Natural Weapons, Imposing Appearance twice, Large Horns (tusks), Herd Leader and Ferocity (defending the herd), Presence +1 and Communication -4, Brawl (tusks) 5 and Leadership (elephants) 5; tusks Init +1, Attack +9, Defense +5, Damage +13. The war elephant: add Aggressive and Pack Animal, Brawl (stomp) 5; stomp Init -2, Attack +6, Defense +3, Damage +13. Persian ones wear the like of leather or metal scale (3 or more to Soak) and carry a howdah for up to six soldiers with javelins, polearms or bows, fighting as a Trained Group with them under the mahout.

Story seeds:
Elephants of Alexander: the bones at ancient battlefields can call back war elephants' ghosts, which interest House Tremere; faerie elephants of Hind, many-tusked and swinging spiked balls, still roam the far eastern mountains and Persia's southern deserts.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 173

creatures.name: The Heavenly Horse of Farghana
creatures.how_many: herds in the valley of Farghana

powers.name: Heavenly Hooves
powers.description: Always active: it runs at full speed whatever the ground, up to thirty miles a day, even over open water or chasms without slowing. ReAn (Base 10, +2 Sun, +1 constant); a Personal Power.

vis.where: a year, faerie-tainted, in the bloody sweat gathered from it

creatures.appearance: Like other middling chargers, a little under sixteen hands high, but finer-boned than the best mundane horse; even a skilled trainer struggles to tell its breeding.
creatures.notes:
The horses of the headwaters of the Jaxartes, famous since ancient times, said to be foals of mortal mares by river dragons or other heavenly steeds; they look much like the Arab-bred horses of Europe's nobles, if a little larger. Magi and Gifted sahirs want them because neither The Gift nor Magical Air troubles them, not even a Blatant Gift, and tales tell of envoys from Serica travelling vast distances for one.

They sweat blood after any hard effort, without harm; a year's sweat, properly gathered, is a vis source of 1 pawn of faerie-tainted Animal vis (its External Vis). As a faerie it neither tires nor ages, but suffers as usual without air, food and water in its role. Like any horse it has +3 to running and jumping. Positive Reputation, which the catalog lacks, is left out. Not balanced as a player's character. Its Abilities are the book's Pretenses.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 174

creatures.name: Ruq
creatures.how_many: roosting in the diamond-strewn valleys of the Roof of the World

powers.name: Clasp
powers.description: Weakens the arms of someone held in its talons after a Grapple, so he cannot struggle free by opposing the Grapple; a Lesser Power, ReCo (Base 3, +2 Sun, +1 Eye).

powers.name: Paralyzing Stare
powers.description: Holds fast any target of human size who meets its terrible stare. ReCo (Base 5, +1 Eye, +1 Concentration); a Lesser Power, cheapened.

creatures.appearance: A gigantic eagle with eyes bright as steel and cruel hooked talons. This is one of the smaller ones, a little over 25 feet tall with a wingspan over 40; bigger ruqs (Size +8) have been seen bearing off elephants and even giants.
creatures.notes:
The roc, which lifts a man in one claw like a mouse and carries off livestock, horses and people. Splendid, but no Beast of Virtue, and not meant as a player's character: built on a big falcon or eagle (Size -2) of base Might 15, raised to giant size. Tough Feathers, which the catalog lacks, is entered as Thick Fur/Thick Scales. The Turks and Mongols of the steppe hunt foxes, and even wolves, with the burkit, a golden eagle of Size -2.

Story seeds:
The Ruq's Nest: faerie ruqs carry those they seize into strange tales far away, as Sinbad was; valleys under their nests are said to be strewn with fist-sized diamonds holding Faerie-tainted vis.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 176

creatures.name: Steppe Pony
creatures.how_many: the nomads' herds; most horses of the eastern provinces
creatures.appearance: A little smaller than Europe's horses, light grey to dappled brown, and very hardy.
creatures.notes: The tarpan of the steppe, bred from its wild horses by every nomad tribe, and unlike the bigger breeds of Europe, Arabia and southern Persia (the Book of Mundane Beasts; Lords of Men, ch. 5). The nomads value most the ponies that have Great Bearer and Sure Traveler, Minor Heroic Virtues (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages pp. 105-107). Like all light horses it has +3 to running and jumping.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 179

creatures.name: Lesser Steppe Spirit
creatures.how_many: one genius loci for each stretch of steppe, from a small valley to a land the size of a kingdom
creatures.notes:
A template, not a full block. Might 30 to 45, of Auram or Terram, or now and then Aquam or Herbam; the pack enters the lowest, in Auram. Each is the genius loci of its own steppe, and all have Ways of the Steppe. Their usual powers are Creator of Winds or of Earth, Guide, Manifestation, Presence, and Ruler of Winds or of Earth, and some can give Major Supernatural Virtues to messengers they choose.

They are fragments of Great Tengri, the sky god the steppe peoples call their common forefather: to Hermetic eyes an Elder Daimon, a Kosmokrator of steppe and sky drawing on the Magic realm, much as the old spirit of the Hercynian Forest does in the west. Where farmers and the Dominion press on the steppe's fringes, Tengri has spent some of its own power to make these lesser spirits. Each meets one of three ends: it holds out, keeping a magical steppe (the plains by the Sea of Azov, the Dzungarian basin, Mongolia's far east); it fades away, leaving mundane grassland, as in Pannonia and the Hungarian plain; or another being takes its place, most often making a faerie steppe.

Story seeds:
The Ride of the Shaman: a character drawn alone onto the steppe by visions survives a killing night and is made a shaman of the Great Tengri, at a Crisis of ageing and two Warping, gaining the Nightwalker's spirit travel and the Pagan Flaw.
The Founder's Final Work: the Great Tengri, untouched by Mercurian rites or the Dominion, is a vast store of magic for a magus who would finish Hercynius's work of bringing Merinita's nature magic into Hermetic theory.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 181

creatures.name: Saluqi
creatures.how_many: packs, or one hunting beside a falcon
creatures.notes:
The noble greyhound-like hound of the Bedouin. Dogs are unclean to most Muslims outside the Maliki school, but saluqis are treasured, sleep in their owners' tents and are mourned in verse, prized for beauty and hunting alike as coursers in fast packs or as bird dogs working with falcons (Lords of Men, ch. 5, on hunting with hounds).

No block of its own: take the greyhound (Realms of Power: Magic p. 143, or the Book of Mundane Beasts), add Grapple, Imposing Appearance twice and Keen Eyesight, drop Keen Sense of Smell, add Endurance and another Improved Characteristics, raise Presence to +1 and Stamina to +3, and make it Hunt 4 (track by sight). Exceptional ones have Puissant Hunt and powers like the Faerie Hounds of Realms of Power: Faerie pp. 88-89.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 104

creatures.name: Saqr
creatures.how_many: kept by falconers across Arabia
creatures.notes:
The Arab falconers' usual bird, like the gyrfalcon and prized for stamina more than speed; the falconers fly it at houbara, stone curlew and hare in the winter. A fine bird, especially a female, marks a tribal leader's standing.

No block of its own: take the gyrfalcon of the Book of Mundane Beasts (Realms of Power: Magic p. 142, or Lords of Men p. 59) and add Tireless and Long-Winded. Exceptional saqrs, the nomad sheikhs' pride, have Puissant Hunt and Imposing Appearance twice.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 106

creatures.name: Shahin
creatures.how_many: kept by falconers across Arabia
creatures.notes:
The peregrine falcon, sometimes preferred to the saqr: the fastest falcon, but with far less stamina, best at taking small birds on the wing and less fit for hawking in the desert.

No block of its own: take the falcon of the Book of Mundane Beasts at Size -4, with Quickness +1 and Strength -2, Ambush Predator, Stealth 3 (ambush prey) and Flight 3 (climbing flight), its combat worked out again to match.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 106

creatures.name: Dromedary
creatures.how_many: in every Bedouin camp and Arabian caravan
creatures.notes:
The one-humped camel the Bedouin use in war and trade, commoner than the Bactrian in North Africa, Egypt, Arabia and the Levant. Magi of Hermes pp. 10-11 gives it in full.

No block of its own: take the Bactrian camel and lower Strength to +1 and Stamina to +3, raise Dexterity to 0, drop Long-Winded, Feral Scent and Hardy and one Fatigue level, make its Reputation Cranky +1 (much of Arabia), its kick Init 0, Atk +4, Dfn +2, Dam +2, its Soak +3, and its Survival 3 (home terrain).
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 104

creatures.name: Arabian Racehorse
creatures.how_many: bred by the Bedouin
creatures.notes:
The Bedouin's famous horses, revered only below the camel. The jinn among them may ride stranger mounts: giant ostriches, leopards, or worse.

No block of its own: take the courser of the Book of Mundane Beasts (Realms of Power: Magic, or the Atlas Games website), add Imposing Appearance twice and Great Quickness, with Presence +1 and Quickness +3. Arabian steeds for war or other work start from the destrier or the charger with the same changes.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 104

creatures.name: Flying Serpent (Iaculus)
creatures.how_many: flocks, in the incense trees of Hadramawt and on Soqotra
creatures.notes:
The syrenii of Pliny, called iaculi by magi and javelin-snakes or darters by most people: white snakes with bat's wings, some with a pair of stubby legs, that perch in the incense trees and dart down on whatever passes. They guard the resin trees, and harvesters drive them off with the smoke of storax brought from Anatolia. Each year flocks try to cross into Egypt and are killed by the ibis, their natural enemy; since the ibis is Thoth's and so Hermes', most magi think them ill-omened, though one Quaesitor uses them in his inquiries.

The book prints no statistics. Exceptional ones are said to slip past wards to deliver their venom, a claim no magus has tested. They are less sociable than the magical Olibanum Serpents of Soqotra (Rival Magic p. 110) and resist taming without magic; which came first is unknown.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 117

creatures.name: Mongol Trooper
creatures.how_many: the horde's vanguard, scouts and guards
creatures.equipment: Composite bow (Load 2), half-armour of metal-reinforced leather (Load 2), saber (Load 1), daggers, spear (Load 1).
creatures.appearance: A fierce horseman of the east, his chest lightly armoured in fur-lined leather under an acorn-shaped iron helmet trimmed with fur, a bow in a saddle quiver, a saber and a short spear with a little hook below the blade.
creatures.notes:
A mundane Mongol of the host now in Transoxiana and eastern Persia, as his victims see him (first given in another form in Ancient Magic pp. 15-18). Younger men ride too; this is the best the characters are likely to meet, a vanguard fighter, or a lone scout or sentry. Bows 5 and Ride 3 each gain +2 from Puissant; Soak is his armour and Stamina. No Confidence is printed. Mongol generals are chiefly brilliant soldiers, not the khan's kin, masters of reading a field and of the feigned retreat that draws a foe into a long, tiring chase before they turn on him.

The orlock (a general): an older companion built from this template, about 40, with Intelligence 0, Perception +1, Presence +2, Communication +1, Strength 0, Stamina +2, Dexterity +1, Quickness 0 (from Improved Characteristics); adding Affinity with Leadership, Clear Thinker, Improved Characteristics, Inspirational, Puissant Leadership, Self-Confident and Strong-Willed, with Enemies (Mythic Middle East), Outsider and Vow (loyalty to Genghis Khan); without Puissant Bows or Reckless. Confidence 2 (5); Resolute +3, Ruthless +5, Cunning +4; add Leadership 6+2 (battlefield), Intrigue 3 (alliances), Guile 3 (elaborate lies), Folk Ken 2 (nobles), Persian 3 (negotiations), Craft: Siege Equipment 3 (catapults or mangonels) and Artes Liberales 1 (military communication); no Bargain, and Bows only 5. Soak, Fatigue, wounds, equipment and Encumbrance stay; combat is worked out again.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 180

creatures.name: Mongol Spirit Shaman
creatures.how_many: a few among the horde
creatures.equipment: Composite bow (Load 2), half-armour of metal-reinforced leather (Load 2), saber (Load 1), daggers, spear (Load 1).
creatures.appearance: An easterner in a jumble of tattered cloth, feathers and beads, with a ritual drum and stick; look closely and his clothes are on inside out.
creatures.notes:
One of the few tribal shamans of Great Tengri, the Mongols' sky god, who ride with the army. Skilled in the spirit world, they call spirits to scout, to fight supernatural foes and to spy, and use whatever kind serves, demons included: a spirit may agree to be bound into a weapon, as a kind of enchanted device, or be set a task. For simplicity, assume he can readily call any suitable spirit, Faerie, Magic or Infernal, up to Might 30, and strike a bargain for its help; the Solomonic summoning rules of ch03 can guide play, and Realms of Power: The Infernal pp. 114-115 has fuller ones. Summoning is the Goetic Art (score 22, an Art).

Every shaman has a familiar spirit much like a qareen, usually an ancestor of his homeland that follows and helps him (his Ghostly Warder; The Mysteries: Revised Edition or Realms of Power: Magic give examples). Each Characteristic except Communication carries 1 aging point; Decrepitude 1 (5). Unlike the shamans of Ancient Magic p. 18.
creatures.source: The Cradle and the Crescent p. 181

calendar.title: The Majlis al-Sulayman
calendar.note: The Order of Suleiman's council meets in its hidden hall in Baghdad's summer bazaar for three days: from dusk on the day the sun passes from Leo into Virgo, as its astrologers reckon to match the First Council, breaking up before dusk of the third day; in 1220 that is 15 to 17 August. Only viziers sit, each vouched for by an Asala, with one vote apiece, usually given by acclaim or a show of hands; all five Asalat must be present, and they settle ties and disputed votes. The new grand vizier's first act is to confirm the judgements made since the last meeting.
